name: p3-0304-class-scope
title: A class body is not a scope for its methods: classscope3 prints 2 and 3
spec: A nested box diagram of classscope3.py. Outer box 'module: X = 1'. Inside it 'def nester(): X = 2  (enclosing function scope E)'. Inside that 'class C: X = 3  (class attribute C.X)'. Inside that 'def method1(self): print(X) ; print(self.X)'. Two lookup arrows from method1. Arrow 1 'print(X): unqualified name follows LEGB, skips the class, finds X in nester: prints 2' (orange). Arrow 2 'print(self.X): goes through self, the inheritance search reaches C.X: prints 3'. Right panel 'Rules': 'a class body runs in its own local namespace, which becomes the class's attribute dictionary', 'a class is not an enclosing scope for the methods inside it', 'methods reach class attributes through self.attr or ClassName.attr', 'class attributes are shared, assigning through an instance only shadows them: node.cluster = x creates an instance attribute and Node.cluster stays the same', 'a list or dict defined at class level is shared by every instance; create per-instance mutable state in __init__'. Bottom bar: 'A class body holds names, but it is not a place a method can see'.
alt: Nested scopes for classscope3.py where print(X) in a method finds the enclosing function's X equal to 2 while print(self.X) finds the class attribute 3, with the class attribute sharing rules.
cap: An unqualified name inside a method skips the class body, so it prints 2, while self.X reaches the class attribute 3.

name: p3-0304-bound-method
title: What node.drain really is: a bound method with __self__ and __func__
spec: A diagram around class Hack with def doit(self, message): print(message). Left 'Hack.doit': the plain function stored on the class; calling needs the instance: Hack.doit(inst, privit). Right 'inst.doit': a bound method object holding two fields, 'meth.__self__ is inst' and 'meth.__func__ is Hack.doit'; 'meth(bonjour)' works like a plain function with self already filled in (orange); can be stored in a callback list. A step line 'I2.w() becomes C3.w(I2): the instance becomes the first argument, received as self; Employee.giveRaise(pat) performs both steps by hand'. Lower panel 'Where an assignment stores a name': 'X = 11 at module top creates a module global manynames.X', 'X = 22 inside g() is local to that call', 'X = 33 inside class C becomes a class attribute C.X, which I.X inherits', 'self.X = 55 inside def m(self) creates an instance attribute in I.__dict__[X]'; links 'I.__class__ points to the class, C.__bases__ holds the direct superclasses'. Footer 'the class statement is executable: it creates a class object that is itself an instance of type; calling the class runs __new__ to allocate and __init__ to initialize'. Bottom bar: 'Methods are ordinary functions stored on the class'.
alt: A plain function on the class beside a bound method object that holds __self__ and __func__, with the four places an assignment of X can store a name.
cap: Reaching a method through an instance wraps the class function with the instance, and where you assign a name decides which namespace holds it.

name: p3-0304-name-mangling
title: Name mangling: two __X attributes that survive side by side
spec: A diamond-free multiple inheritance diagram. Class C1 with 'self.__X = 88 in meth1'. Class C2 with 'self.__X = 99 in metha'. Class 'C3(C1, C2): pass' below both. Compile step labels 'inside a class body the compiler rewrites __X to _ClassName__X': C1 stores _C1__X, C2 stores _C2__X. Instance dictionary box: "{'_C1__X': 88, '_C2__X': 99}" both values survive because the names differ (orange). Access note 'I._C1__X is still readable: mangling prevents collisions in deep hierarchies, it does not prevent deliberate access, much as Java private fields can be read through setAccessible(True) reflection'. Convention panel 'single leading underscore _name: only a convention for internal; double leading underscore __X: mangled; Python trusts programmers, document the public API and leave the rest to convention'. Bottom bar: 'Mangling avoids accidental collisions between subclasses'.
alt: Classes C1 and C2 each storing a double underscore X that is rewritten to _C1__X and _C2__X, so the C3 instance dictionary holds 88 and 99 together.
cap: The compiler rewrites each double underscore name with its class name, so two classes can use __X without colliding.

name: p3-0304-slots-rules
title: __slots__: four rules that decide whether the memory saving is real
spec: A table with four rules, each with a one line example and the failure. 'Rule 1 every class in the hierarchy defines __slots__': class C: pass; class D(C): __slots__ = [a] still gives D() an instance __dict__; a subclass that adds no new attributes still declares __slots__ = (). 'Rule 2 do not repeat slot names in subclasses': instances inherit the union of all __slots__ along the MRO; repeating a superclass slot hides its descriptor and wastes space. 'Rule 3 a slot name cannot have a class-level default': class C: __slots__ = [a]; a = 99 raises ValueError: a in __slots__ conflicts with class variable; under multiple inheritance at most one base may have a non-empty __slots__, else TypeError: multiple bases have instance lay-out conflict, so mixins use __slots__ = (). 'Rule 4 slotted instances have no __dict__ unless __dict__ is listed in __slots__' and 'obj.__slots__ shows only the lowest class's list, so generic tools use dir(obj) and getattr(obj, name)'. Headline numbers panel (orange) 'Vector2d with __slots__ = (__x, __y): 10 million instances shrink from 1.62 GiB to 655 MiB in mem_test.py'. Intro strip 'assigning a sequence of attribute names to __slots__ reserves fixed storage per instance; class-level descriptors manage it; no per-instance __dict__ or __weakref__'. Bottom bar: 'Reach for __slots__ when millions of instances exist, and keep __init__ cheap'.
alt: Four rules for __slots__ with examples of the failures, such as a superclass without slots, repeated names, a class default conflict and a missing __dict__, plus the 1.62 GiB to 655 MiB result.
cap: Every class in the hierarchy must declare slots, or the per-instance dictionary quietly returns and the memory saving disappears.

name: p3-0304-vector2d-habits
title: Five habits of a well-built domain object, shown on Vector2d
spec: A five row table 'Habit', 'Code', 'What it gives you'. '1 __iter__ returns (i for i in (self.x, self.y))' / 'x, y = v1 and tuple(self) work automatically'. '2 __repr__ uses "{}({!r}, {!r})".format(type(self).__name__, *self)' / 'eval(repr(v1)) == v1 holds, and subclasses inherit the right class name'. '3 __bytes__ plus classmethod frombytes(cls, octets)' / 'bytes([ord(self.typecode)]) + bytes(array(self.typecode, self)); frombytes reads typecode = chr(octets[0]); memv = memoryview(octets[1:]).cast(typecode); return cls(*memv)'. '4 custom __format__(self, fmt_spec)' / 'a p suffix for polar coordinates: format(Vector2d(1, 1), 0.5fp) == <1.41421, 0.78540>'. '5 hashable and immutable' / 'read-only @property getters backed by self.__x and self.__y; __hash__ returns hash((self.x, self.y)); __match_args__ = (x, y) allows case Vector2d(0, 0):; __slots__ = (__x, __y)'. Side example 'typecode = d (an 8-byte IEEE 754 float) is a class attribute read through self.typecode; change one instance with v1.typecode = f, or subclass: class ShortVector2d(Vector2d): typecode = f (a 4-byte float)' (orange). Footer '@property keeps callers writing node.state while validation happens behind the name; start with plain attributes and add a property later; also functools.cached_property for lazy computation; keep __init__ cheap, no IO'. Bottom bar: 'Copy these five habits into your own classes'.
alt: A table of five Vector2d habits, __iter__, a subclass-friendly __repr__, __bytes__ with frombytes, a polar __format__ and a hashable immutable design, with what each gives.
cap: Each Vector2d method enables a built-in behaviour such as unpacking, eval round-trips, binary encoding, formatting or hashing.

name: p3-0304-record-evolution
title: From a dict record to a Person class: what each step adds
spec: A four step staircase. Step 1 'dict record: rec = {}; rec[name] = Pat; rec[age] = 40.5; rec[jobs] = [dev, mgr]; holds data, no room for logic'. Step 2 'class as namespace: class rec: pass; rec.name = Pat; less syntax, but a new class for every distinct record'. Step 3 'instances of an empty class: pers1 = rec(); pers1.name = Bob; pers2 = rec(); pers2.name = Sue; the two records do not need the same names, only pers1 has an age'. Step 4 (orange) 'class with constructor and methods: Person.__init__(self, name, jobs, age=None); info() returns (self.name, self.jobs); rec1 = Person(Bob, [dev, mgr], 40.5); rec2 = Person(Sue, [dev, cto]); every record consistent, with processing logic'. Side panel 'Under the hood: namespaces are dictionaries': 'rec.__dict__ holds name and age (class); x.__dict__ is {name: Sue}; y.__dict__ is []', 'x.age finds 40 by inheritance, but x.__dict__[age] raises KeyError: indexing sees only what the object holds directly, dot notation runs the inheritance search', 'dir(x) collects inherited names too: [age, name]', 'x.__class__ is the class rec, rec.__bases__ is (object,)', 'rec.method = uppername makes a plain function a method: x.method() and rec.method(x) both return SUE'. Bottom bar: 'When an attribute surprises you, ask which namespace holds it'.
alt: Four steps from a dictionary record to a class namespace, instances of an empty class and a Person class with a constructor, with __dict__ and dot lookup differences.
cap: A class packages the data of a record with its logic, and dot lookup climbs the class tree while __dict__ indexing does not.

name: p3-0304-super-rules
title: Cooperative super(): the D to B to C to A chain and how one missing call breaks it
spec: A diamond. A at the top with f returning A. B(A) and C(A) below it. D(B, C) at the bottom. Chain arrows along the MRO 'D.__mro__ = (D, B, C, A, object)'. Output 'D().f() returns D>B>C>A'. Each f: 'A.f returns A', 'B.f returns B> + super().f()', 'C.f returns C> + super().f()', 'D.f returns D> + super().f()'. Note 'super() returns a proxy to the next class in the instance's MRO after the class that contains the call, which is not always the direct parent'. C3 rule strip 'children before parents, parents keep the order you declared, each class appears once; in a diamond the shared base is reached once after all its subclasses'. Right panel 'Three rules for cooperative inheritance': '1 universal deployment: every class that implements the method before the anchor must call super().method(); the first class that omits it stops the chain; if class C(B, A) calls super().act() and B.act does not, A.act is never reached' (orange); '2 anchors: the chain must end at a class that defines the method without calling super() again; object is the anchor for __init__; for a custom act(self), super().act() in the last class before object raises AttributeError: super object has no attribute act; a common base with its own act must sit before object'; '3 compatible signatures: each implementation consumes its own keyword arguments and forwards **kwargs; object.__init__ accepts nothing beyond self, so TypeError: object.__init__() takes exactly one argument'. Bottom bar: 'Check __mro__ before you trust a super() chain'.
alt: A diamond of A, B, C and D whose MRO gives D then B then C then A, with the three rules for cooperative super calls: every class calls super, the chain ends at an anchor and signatures are compatible.
cap: super() follows the MRO rather than the direct parent, so every class on the chain must pass the call along.

name: p3-0304-subclass-ways
title: Four ways a subclass talks to its superclass, plus mixins and delegation
spec: A table of four patterns from specialize.py with Super. 'Inheritor(Super): pass, inherits methods unchanged'. 'Replacer(Super): overrides method(self) completely'. 'Extender(Super): overrides method(self) and calls back Super.method(self); example Manager.giveRaise(self, percent, bonus=.10) calls Person.giveRaise(self, percent + bonus)'. 'Provider(Super): implements the abstract action(self) hook that Super.delegate(self) expects, the Template Method pattern' (orange). Below, 'Mixins': 'a small class named ...Mixin adding one independent capability through multiple inheritance: AttrDisplay, ListInstance (inspects self.__dict__), ListInherited (dir(self)), ListTree (climbs __class__ and __bases__); UpperCaseMixin uppercases string keys with super().__setitem__(_upper(key), item) and must be listed first: class UpperDict(UpperCaseMixin, collections.UserDict): pass, so it intercepts calls before UserDict on the MRO'. Warning 'subclassing a built-in C type such as dict or list directly is risky because C methods ignore Python overrides; use collections.UserDict, UserList or UserString'. 'Composition and delegation': 'inheritance models is-a (PizzaRobot is a Chef, a Chef is an Employee); composition models has-a (PizzaShop contains Server, PizzaRobot and Oven; Department gathers Person and Manager objects); delegation: a wrapper holds an embedded object and forwards requests with def __getattr__(self, attr): return getattr(self.person, attr); special operators such as __str__ or __add__ are looked up on the class directly, so they bypass instance-level __getattr__'. Bottom strip 'isinstance(x, Base) and issubclass respect inheritance; type(x) is T checks the exact type, rarely wanted; Liskov: a subclass accepts at least what the base accepts, returns no less than the base promises, and adds no surprising exceptions'. Bottom bar: 'Customize a component without touching its source'.
alt: A table of Inheritor, Replacer, Extender and Provider subclass patterns, with mixin ordering on the MRO, the UserDict advice and delegation through __getattr__.
cap: A subclass can inherit, replace, extend or fill in a hook, and mixins must come first on the MRO to intercept calls.

name: p3-0304-abc-vs-protocol
title: ABC, virtual subclass, structural ABC or Protocol: which check applies
spec: A decision tree. Question 'Do you control the hierarchy and want shared concrete code and runtime enforcement?' yes (orange) 'ABC: Provider(ABC) with @abstractmethod create_vm, delete_vm, find and a concrete template method ensure_vm returning self.find(name) or self.create_vm(name, cpus); a subclass that forgets an abstract method cannot be instantiated: TypeError at creation, not at the first call'. no 'Are the implementers third-party or unrelated, at a boundary?' yes 'Protocol: Sink with write(self, data: bytes) -> int; flush_to(sink, data) accepts files, sockets, BytesIO and your own classes; static checkers verify conformance; @runtime_checkable allows isinstance but only checks that the methods exist; fakes need no inheritance'. Side column 'Other mechanisms': 'virtual subclass: @Tombola.register class TomboList(list), verified by TomboList.__mro__ versus Tombola._abc_registry; Provider.register(Third)'; 'structural ABC: collections.abc.Sized checks __subclasshook__ for a __len__ entry in the class's __mro__ dictionaries, so class Struggle with def __len__(self): return 23 satisfies isinstance(Struggle(), abc.Sized) with no inheritance or register()'; 'Tombola(ABC) abstract load(iterable) and pick(); pick raises LookupError when empty (parent of IndexError and KeyError); concrete loaded() and inspect(); BingoCage and LottoBlower implement it'; 'goose typing (Alex Martelli) versus duck typing, static nominal typing and static duck typing through typing.Protocol'. Story 'a refactor splits one storage client into two, and isinstance checks still name the old class; the tests pass for reasons that have nothing to do with what the code needs; a protocol describes the interface by the methods an object has'. Bottom bar: 'Use an ABC to enforce, a Protocol to keep coupling loose'.
alt: A decision tree choosing between an ABC with abstract methods and a template method, a structural Protocol for third-party boundaries, virtual subclass registration and the Sized subclasshook.
cap: Use an ABC when you own the hierarchy and want enforcement at instantiation, and a Protocol when implementers are unrelated or third-party.

name: p3-0304-builders-table
title: Data class builders compared: mutability, typing, validation
spec: A table with columns 'Builder', 'Mutable?', 'Typing', 'Validation', 'Notes' and six rows. 'collections.namedtuple("P", "x y")' / 'No (tuple)' / 'Untyped' / 'None' / 'lightweight, tuple behaviour; same memory as a plain tuple, field names live on the class in City._fields; _make(iterable), _asdict(), defaults=(...) for the rightmost fields'. 'typing.NamedTuple' / 'No' / 'Typed fields' / 'None' / 'class syntax, defaults, methods'. '@dataclasses.dataclass' / 'Yes, or frozen=True' / 'Typed annotations, not enforced' / 'via __post_init__' / 'standard library, most common'. 'attrs (@define)' / 'Yes or frozen' / 'Optional' / 'validators and converters' / 'third party, predates dataclasses'. 'pydantic.BaseModel' (orange) / 'Yes or frozen' / 'Enforced at runtime, coercion' / 'strong, with errors' / 'parsing external data, settings, FastAPI'. 'TypedDict' / 'A dict' / 'Static only' / 'None' / 'types JSON-like dicts, no runtime class'. Annotation behaviour strip 'plain class: a: int exists only in __annotations__, DemoPlainClass.a raises AttributeError; NamedTuple: a and b become read-only tuple fields; dataclass: a and b become mutable instance attributes with generated __init__(self, a: int, b: float = 1.1) -> None; in all three the unannotated c = spam stays a class attribute; all three generate __match_args__ for case City(continent=Asia, name=_, country=cc):'. Bottom bar: 'Pick the lightest builder that gives the checks you need'.
alt: A table of namedtuple, NamedTuple, dataclass, attrs, pydantic BaseModel and TypedDict by mutability, typing and validation, with how annotations behave in plain, NamedTuple and dataclass classes.
cap: Only pydantic enforces types at runtime, and dataclasses validate through __post_init__, while namedtuples and TypedDicts do not validate at all.

name: p3-0304-dataclass-options
title: GpuNode as a frozen dataclass: options and the three quiet pitfalls
spec: The decorator line '@dataclass(order=True, frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only=True)' with each option explained. 'frozen=True: instances immutable and hashable together with eq; use replace(n, gpus=4) for a modified copy'. 'order=True: sorted([n2, n]) compares by field order'. 'slots=True (3.10+)'. 'kw_only=True: helps when a non-default field would follow a default one'. Fields strip 'name: str, rack: str, gpus: int = 8, tags: tuple[str, ...] = (), MAX_GPUS: ClassVar[int] = 16 (class variable, not a field)'. '__post_init__ validation: 0 < gpus <= MAX_GPUS else ValueError(gpus out of range)'. 'Cluster: nodes: list[GpuNode] = field(default_factory=list), meta: dict = field(default_factory=dict); NEVER default=[] because dataclasses reject mutable defaults' (orange). Extras 'field(default_factory, repr=False, compare=False, init=False, metadata={...}), InitVar for init-only parameters, dataclasses.fields(obj), asdict(n) recursive for JSON'. ClassVar example 'HackerClubMember: all_handles: ClassVar[set[str]] = set() is not turned into an instance field; __post_init__ fills self.handle = self.name.split()[0] when empty and raises ValueError if the handle is already in cls.all_handles'. Pitfalls panel 'annotations are not enforced: GpuNode(name=5) succeeds, validate in __post_init__ or use pydantic at the boundaries', 'a frozen dataclass is only shallowly immutable: a list inside can still change, use tuples or frozensets', 'equality compares every field by default; use compare=False for fields that change often'. Bottom bar: 'A Data Class with no behaviour can be a code smell when its logic is scattered across callers'.
alt: The options of a frozen ordered slotted keyword-only dataclass for GpuNode, default_factory for Cluster, ClassVar and __post_init__ examples, and three pitfalls.
cap: frozen, order, slots and kw_only change the generated class, default_factory avoids shared lists, and annotations are never enforced at runtime.

name: p3-0304-pydantic-flow
title: Pydantic at the boundary: what happens to a node spec arriving from YAML
spec: A left to right flow. Input box 'dict from YAML: {name: gpu01, ip: 10.0.0.5, gpus: "8"}' (gpus quoted as a string). Arrow into 'NodeSpec.model_validate(...)' box listing model rules 'extra: forbid, frozen: True', 'name: str with pattern ^[a-z0-9-]+$ and max_length 63, plus a field_validator rejecting localhost and admin', 'ip: IPv4Address', 'gpus: int, default 8, ge 1, le 16', 'role: Literal[compute, login, storage] default compute'. Two outcomes. Success branch 'gpus string 8 is coerced to int 8; spec.model_dump(), model_dump_json(), NodeSpec.model_json_schema()'. Failure branch (orange) 'a typo such as timout instead of timeout is rejected at once because extra is forbid; ValidationError with e.errors(): a structured list of errors with locations, so you can report exactly which field is wrong; the error arrives at the person who wrote the file'. Settings panel 'class Settings(BaseSettings): env_prefix MYOPS_, env_file .env; api_url: str, api_token: SecretStr (repr shows **********, call .get_secret_value() deliberately), timeout: float = 10.0'. Footer 'v2 uses a Rust core, v1 has a different API; nested, generic and discriminated unions Field(discriminator=type), computed fields; FastAPI uses them for request and response schemas (chapter 3.7)'. Bottom bar: 'Validate once at the boundary, then pass trusted typed objects through the rest of the code'.
alt: A node spec with a quoted gpus value validated by a pydantic model, coerced to an integer on success and rejected with a structured error on an unknown key, plus BaseSettings with SecretStr.
cap: Pydantic coerces a quoted 8 to an integer, rejects unknown keys such as a misspelled timeout at once and returns structured errors.

name: p3-0304-variance
title: Invariant, covariant and contravariant generics, with the bin and the dispenser
spec: Three columns. Column 'Invariant: T = TypeVar(T)' (orange): 'list[Dog] cannot be used as list[Animal]', 'because a caller could append a Cat to a mutable list[Animal]'. Column 'Covariant: T_co = TypeVar(T_co, covariant=True)': 'read-only producers: Sequence[T_co], Iterator[T_co], BeverageDispenser[T_co]', 'varies in the same direction: BeverageDispenser[OrangeJuice] is a subtype of BeverageDispenser[Juice]'. Column 'Contravariant: T_contra = TypeVar(T_contra, contravariant=True)': 'write-only consumers: TrashCan[T_contra]', 'varies in the opposite direction: TrashCan[Refuse] is a subtype of TrashCan[Biodegradable], because a general refuse bin can safely accept biodegradable trash'. Callable strip 'Callable[[int, str], bool] is contravariant in its argument types and covariant in its return type; Callable[[float], None] is a subtype of Callable[[int], None]: a callback that handles any float can safely handle an int; the reverse does not hold; for keyword or variadic arguments define a Protocol with __call__'. Bounds strip 'LT = TypeVar(LT, bound=SupportsLessThan) with class SupportsLessThan(Protocol): def __lt__(self, other: Any) -> bool; top(series: Iterable[LT], length: int) -> list[LT]'; 'NumberT = TypeVar(NumberT, float, Decimal, Fraction) limits mode() to those three types'; 'LottoBlower[int](range(1, 11)); Python 3.12 shorter syntax class Stack[T]:'. Bottom bar: 'Producers vary with T, consumers vary against it'.
alt: Three columns for invariant, covariant and contravariant generics with the list of Dog and Animal, the beverage dispenser, the trash can and the Callable argument rule.
cap: Read-only producers are covariant, write-only consumers are contravariant, and a mutable container must be invariant.

name: p3-0304-typing-toolkit
title: Type hint forms and the checker rules that matter most
spec: A table of forms with one line each. 'Iterable[Node] | None (3.10+ union; Optional[X] is X | None): the checker forces you to handle None; narrow with if x is not None, isinstance, assert x or an early return'. 'dict[str, list[Node]] builtin generics (3.9+)'. 'Callable[[], T] with TypeVar T for a function that keeps the type it receives'. 'NewType(Port, int): a distinct type for the checker'. 'Final: MAX_RETRIES: Final = 5'. 'Literal[dry-run, apply]'. 'TypedDict(total=False): the shape of a dict; zero runtime validation, a from_json returning arbitrary JSON passes at runtime unless you validate with pydantic'. 'TypeAlias: JsonScalar = str | int | float | bool | None'. '@overload: several signatures plus one unannotated implementation, for sum and max with or without key= and default='. 'Self types fluent methods and classmethods'. 'Annotated[int, Field(ge=0)] attaches metadata for pydantic and FastAPI'. Rules panel (orange) 'Postel's Law: accept general types (Iterable, Sequence, Mapping), return concrete list or dict; do not annotate a read-only parameter as dict or list when Mapping, Sequence or Iterable will do; name2hex(name: str, color_map: Mapping[str, int]) accepts dict, defaultdict, ChainMap or UserDict'. 'Any versus object: Any is both a subtype and a supertype of every type, so it turns checking off and the effect spreads, as with json.loads(); object accepts any value but allows only operations every object supports until you narrow it; typing.cast and # type: ignore[code] switch off checking for that line'. Gradual strip 'CPython ignores hints at runtime and stores them in __annotations__; mypy, pyright, pyre, pytype read them; unannotated functions are ignored by default; keep fixed-length tuple[str, float, str] separate from tuple[int, ...]; TYPE_CHECKING blocks for annotation-only imports; reveal_type(x); get_type_hints(func) and inspect.signature(func) read lazy annotations'. CI strip 'annotate public APIs first, then mypy --strict, per-module overrides (ignore_missing_imports for redfish.* and paramiko.*), stubgen, types-requests; new errors fail the build'. Bottom bar: 'Typing pays off most at boundaries: API clients, config models and plugin interfaces'.
alt: A table of type hint forms such as unions, NewType, Final, Literal, TypedDict, overload and Annotated, with Postel's Law, Any versus object and a gradual strict-mode rollout.
cap: Annotate general types on parameters and concrete types on returns, treat Any as the off switch, and tighten mypy settings step by step in CI.

name: p3-0304-vector-takes
title: The N-dimensional Vector, one capability at a time (Takes 1 to 5)
spec: A five step ladder. '1 short __repr__ with reprlib.repr: Vector(range(1000)) is truncated, like Vector([0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, ...])'. '2 slice-aware __getitem__: if isinstance(key, slice): return type(self)(self._components[key]); else operator.index(key), which calls __index__ and raises TypeError for floats or tuples; slice.indices(length) normalizes bounds; SkipObject returns a new iterator from each __iter__ call so [x + y for x in skipper for y in skipper] makes 9 pairs from aa to ee, while Squares returns self from __iter__ and scans only once'. '3 dynamic read-only attributes x, y, z, t through __match_args__ and __getattr__ reading self._components[0..3]; trap (orange): v.x = 10 creates v.__dict__[x], which shadows __getattr__ while v[0] stays unchanged; fix: __setattr__ raises AttributeError for single lowercase letters a to z; allowed writes use super().__setattr__(attr, val) to avoid infinite recursion'. '4 hashing: functools.reduce(operator.xor, (hash(x) for x in self), 0), initializer 0 covers empty vectors; streaming equality len(self) == len(other) and all(a == b for a, b in zip(self, other)) in O(1) extra memory'. '5 operators: __neg__, __pos__, __add__, __radd__, __mul__, __rmul__, __matmul__, __rmatmul__, __contains__, __iadd__; format h for hyperspherical coordinates'. Worked results strip 'Vector([3, 4, 5]) + (10, 20) and (10, 20) + Vector([3, 4, 5]) both give Vector([13.0, 24.0, 5.0]) using zip_longest(self, other, fillvalue=0.0) and __radd__ = __add__; adding 1 is rejected cleanly by returning NotImplemented in except TypeError; Vector([1, 2, 3]) @ Vector([4, 5, 6]) == 32.0 after checking isinstance(other, abc.Sized) and Iterable; if __iadd__ is missing, v1 += v2 falls back to v1 = v1 + v2 and changes id(v1), while a mutable class returns self'. Bottom bar: 'If an operator has no natural meaning for your type, give the method a name'.
anchor: ### Sequence special methods (`Vector` Takes #1–#5, Fluent Python Chapter 12) and operator overloading (Fluent Python Chapter 16 and Learning Python Chapter 30)
alt: A five step ladder building an N-dimensional Vector through repr, slicing, dynamic read-only attributes, hashing and operators, with the add, matmul and in-place worked results.
cap: Each take adds one capability, and the attribute and in-place operator traps show why __setattr__ and returning self matter.

name: p3-0304-version-bytes
title: Two domain types: Version sorts like a human, Bytes prints like a human
spec: Two panels. Panel 'Why strings fail': 'release tags 1.9 and 1.10 compared as plain strings: 1.10 comes first, the rollout picks the older image and the bug looks like a build problem for an hour'. Panel 'Version with @total_ordering': '__init__ stores parts = tuple(int(p) for p in s.split("."))', 'so 1.9 becomes (1, 9) and 1.10 becomes (1, 10), and tuple comparison puts (1, 10) after (1, 9)' (orange); 'define __eq__ and __lt__; @total_ordering generates the rest; both return NotImplemented for non-Version operands; __hash__ returns hash(self.parts); __repr__ Version(1.10)'. Panel 'Bytes(int)': 'subclass a builtin for a domain type; __str__ divides by 1024 through B, KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB and prints with one decimal; Bytes(1024) prints 1.0 KiB rather than 1024'. Real tools strip 'real version handling: packaging.version.Version; IP addresses: ipaddress; durations: datetime.timedelta'. Rules strip 'overload an operator only when its meaning is natural (vectors, sizes, versions, durations); return new objects so the value semantics stay clear; return NotImplemented for operand types you do not understand; keep __eq__, __hash__ and ordering methods consistent'. Operator example 'ThirdClass(SecondClass): __add__ returns a new ThirdClass so the result keeps the same type; __str__ gives [ThirdClass: 6] for print; mul changes the instance in place and is a named method; a custom intersection can be intersect() by name or __and__ for &, and plain names are clearer unless your objects truly behave like built-ins'. Bottom bar: 'Compare versions as tuples of integers, never as strings'.
alt: A Version class that compares release tags as tuples of integers so 1.10 sorts after 1.9, and a Bytes class that prints 1.0 KiB, with the rules for overloading operators.
cap: Comparing 1.9 and 1.10 as tuples of integers sorts them as people expect, and total_ordering fills in the other comparisons.

name: p3-0304-provider-layer
title: The typed provider layer: enum, frozen dataclass, Protocol and a fake
spec: A layered diagram. Top 'State(StrEnum): PENDING, RUNNING, STOPPED'. Next 'Instance: frozen, slots dataclass with id, name, state, ip: str | None = None'. Middle 'Compute(Protocol): list_instances(project) -> list[Instance]; start(project, instance_id) -> None'. Left implementer 'a real cloud client'. Right implementer 'FakeCompute: instances and started lists, no inheritance (orange)'. Centre function 'ensure_running(c: Compute, project, names: set[str]) -> list[str]: for inst in c.list_instances(project): if inst.name in names and inst.state is not State.RUNNING: c.start(project, inst.id); started.append(inst.name)'. Test strip 'FakeCompute([Instance(1, a, STOPPED), Instance(2, b, RUNNING)]); ensure_running(fake, p, {a, b}) == [a] and fake.started == [1]: only the stopped instance a needs to start, and no cloud API is touched'. Habits panel with the twelve: '1 functions until state or polymorphism appears', '2 separate IO from logic: functional core, imperative shell', '3 make illegal states unrepresentable: enums, Literals, frozen dataclasses, validation at construction', '4 small explicit interfaces: depend on a two-method Protocol and inject it', '5 immutable configuration and value objects', '6 errors are part of the API: MyOpsError with NodeNotFound beneath it', '7 avoid deep inheritance: one or two levels', '8 enums for fixed choices; auto(), Flag for bit flags', '9 useful __repr__ and log with %r', '10 no global mutable singletons', '11 docstrings and types; deprecate with warnings.warn(..., DeprecationWarning)', '12 SOLID: one responsibility, registries or plugins, contracts, Protocols, injection'. Bottom bar: 'Pass the collaborator in, and the test needs no cloud'.
alt: A layered typed provider design with a StrEnum state, a frozen dataclass Instance, a Compute Protocol, ensure_running and a FakeCompute test, beside the twelve design habits.
cap: Because FakeCompute satisfies the Compute Protocol without inheriting from it, ensure_running is tested with no cloud API.

name: p3-0304-mistakes
title: Ten class and typing mistakes with their fixes
spec: A two column table 'Mistake' and 'Fix'. 'Mutable class attributes and mutable default arguments; forgetting default_factory in a dataclass' / 'create state in __init__; field(default_factory=list)'. 'Deep inheritance; inconsistent super().__init__ calls breaking cooperative inheritance; overriding methods with different signatures' / 'one or two levels, composition, compatible signatures'. 'Classes as namespaces for functions, where a module is the right tool, or as singletons' / 'a module and module-level objects'. 'Assuming type hints enforce anything at runtime; sprinkling Any and unchecked # type: ignore' / 'run mypy or pyright in CI; validate at the boundary with pydantic'. 'Validating the same data over and over, or never' / 'validate once at the boundary'. 'Exposing mutable internals such as returning the internal list' / 'return copies or tuples'. 'Overloading operators with surprising semantics, or __eq__ without __hash__' / 'natural meanings only; keep them consistent'. 'IO in __init__, or catching exceptions in constructors and leaving half-initialized objects' / 'explicit factory classmethod or lazy connection'. 'Pickling untrusted data, or relying on __del__' (orange) / 'JSON, YAML or protobuf; __enter__ and __exit__; pickle with __getstate__ is unsafe for untrusted data and breaks across versions'. 'Storing secrets in attributes that repr shows' / 'SecretStr'. Footer 'copy.copy and copy.deepcopy can be customized with __copy__ and __deepcopy__'. Bottom bar: 'Look for each of them in turn when you review your own code'.
alt: A table of ten class and typing mistakes such as mutable class attributes, deep inheritance, assuming hints are enforced, IO in __init__, pickling untrusted data and secrets in repr, each with its fix.
cap: Most of these mistakes are shared state, hidden coupling or unchecked assumptions, and each has a standard fix.
